cra.title: EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) · vulnerability reporting
cra.description: Assess each KEV match on your products; only one exploited in your product starts the reporting deadlines.

help.title: What the CRA asks for
help.scope: It applies to manufacturers that sell products with digital elements in the EU. From 11 September 2026, every vulnerability actively exploited in the product must be reported.
help.deadlines: Deadlines, counted from when you become aware: early warning within 24 h, notification within 72 h, and a final report within 14 days of a corrective measure being available.
help.platform: Reports go through ENISA's single reporting platform, to the coordinating CSIRT and to ENISA. Pitangus doesn't send anything: it prepares the draft and records who marked each stage as sent.
help.exploited: "Actively exploited in your product" means reliable evidence that someone exploited the vulnerability in your product without permission, not just that the CVE is exploited somewhere.
help.kev: A CISA KEV match is only a signal: the CVE is exploited in the wild, but your product may not reach the vulnerable code. Assess it first; the deadlines start when you record that it's exploited in your product.
help.admin_only: Only an admin can mark products, assess events and record what was sent.
